concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 1 - Data Ingestion and Harmonization
concerns.text: User Story 1 has functional requirements (FR-001, FR-002) but no associated Success Criteria. Every story must be backed by at least one SC (see lens rules).
SC-004 references the runtime constraint but does not name a user story it validates. It is an orphaned success criterion.
SC-005 references power‑analysis reporting but no user story is linked; it is an orphaned success criterion.

The Edge Cases section states “The system MUST perform power analysis and report calculated power and margin of error,” yet no functional requirement (FR‑xxx) captures this capability. A missing FR creates a gap in the functional spec.
FR-001 (and other FRs) reference "US-1" (e.g., "(See US-1)") but the document defines the user stories as "User Story 1" etc. The identifier "US-1" does not exist, causing a broken cross‑reference.
Inconsistent terminology: the narrative uses "User Story 1" while functional requirements use the shorthand "US-1". This unstable naming can lead to confusion and mis‑linking between sections.

concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 3 - high-fiber (top [deferred], 75th percentile) and low-fiber (bottom [deferred], 25th percentile)
concerns.text: The specification defines high‑fiber as the top 75th percentile and low‑fiber as the bottom 25th percentile, whereas the original idea explicitly states high‑fiber = top 25 % and low‑fiber = bottom 25 % (quartiles). This silent redefinition changes the research question and will affect effect‑size estimates and replication criteria.

concerns.location: spec.md:Edge Cases – “What if one dataset has significantly fewer samples than the other? → The system MUST perform power analysis and report calculated power and margin of error.”
concerns.text: The idea does not request a formal power analysis; it only mentions a measurement‑error simulation. Adding a mandatory power‑analysis step introduces work beyond the scoped research question.

concerns.location: spec.md:Success Criteria – SC-004 “Computational feasibility is measured against the constraint of ≤6 hours runtime on a CPU‑only GitHub Actions runner.”
concerns.text: Runtime constraints were not part of the original idea. Introducing a hard 6‑hour limit adds an engineering requirement that was not requested and may unnecessarily restrict implementation choices.

FR-004 requires using MaAsLin2 (or equivalent linear model) on CLR‑transformed taxon abundances. MaAsLin2 already performs its own log‑ratio transformation; applying an additional CLR step may violate the model’s assumptions and constitute double‑transformation of compositional data.

SC-001 asks for a Spearman ρ together with a standard error. Spearman correlation is a non‑parametric rank statistic; a closed‑form standard error is not defined. Reporting a standard error would require bootstrapping or other resampling, which is not specified, making the success criterion ambiguous.

new_concerns.text: FR-003 requires applying CLR transformation to taxon abundance data ("System MUST apply centered log‑ratio (CLR) transformation to taxon abundance data for correlation analysis (See US-2)").

FR-004 states that MaAsLin2 will handle compositional aspects internally and that no prior CLR is needed ("MaAsLin2 will handle compositional aspects internally (no prior CLR)"). This directly contradicts FR-003's requirement to apply CLR beforehand.

FR‑004 states that MaAsLin2 will handle compositional aspects internally and that no prior CLR transformation is needed, while FR‑003 and US‑2 require a CLR transformation before association analysis. This contradiction diverges from the idea, which mandates CLR‑transformed abundances as input to the linear model. The inconsistency may prevent the analysis from correctly addressing the compositional nature of microbiome data.

responses.response: Adjusted the definition of high‑fiber and low‑fiber groups to match the original idea (top 25 % and bottom 25 % of fiber intake). Updated the US‑3 description and added a brief justification in the Assumptions section. All references now use concrete percentile thresholds (≥ 75th percentile for high‑fiber, ≤ 25th percentile for low‑fiber).
responses.what_changed: Replaced vague '[deferred]' placeholders with explicit percentile definitions in US‑3 description; added justification sentence in Assumptions; ensured consistency in acceptance scenario wording.

new_concerns.text: The specification omits the Spearman correlation analysis between fiber intake and CLR‑transformed taxon abundances that was explicitly described in the idea’s methodology sketch. Without this non‑parametric correlation step, the analysis does not fully address the original research question.

The idea includes a measurement‑error simulation/sensitivity analysis to assess bias from self‑reported fiber intake, but the specification provides no corresponding validation or sensitivity component. This omission limits the ability to evaluate robustness of the reported associations.
